name: vimbrowser-cli
systemHint: You can control the user's vimbrowser browser through the `vimbrowser-cli` CLI tool (source at <exocortex-source-dir>/external-tools/vimbrowser-cli). Run `vimbrowser-cli -h` for usage reference. Open and open-context create background tabs; use focus only when the user explicitly requests it. Use `frame-tree` plus frame-html/frame-text/frame-js for exact cross-origin frame inspection. Pass JavaScript and raw IPC payloads on stdin. Use `inspect-controls --frame FRAME` to inspect controls without clicking; it returns short-lived exact-node handles and never picks the first match. Use `activate-control TAB HANDLE` for a one-shot trusted click on that exact inspected node, including controls that require transient user activation such as OAuth popup buttons. Use `pointer TAB HANDLE click --at DX,DY` / `drag --to DX,DY` for a trusted click or drag at CSS offsets inside that node, and `key-input TAB HANDLE` for trusted keys into its focused frame. Use `upload-file ... handle:HANDLE PATH` to activate that exact node and causally supply its chooser. For main-document file controls, direct CSS/index and `activate:SELECTOR` remain available. Target `chooser` remains available for a manual one-shot arm followed by a user click. Never guess among multiple controls, never use screen coordinates, and do not try to read local files from page JavaScript. Use diagnose TAB [--expected-origin URL] for read-only transport/UI/target/build/auth evidence; it never wakes or focuses tabs and keeps historical timeout cause and unprobed renderer readiness unknown. A timeout is not rollback: never blindly retry mutations. Use open-context --brief CONTEXT URL for an opt-in exact-created-tab response on the new browser. CLI --timeout is seconds; check the outer tool schema separately (timeout_seconds is seconds).
